Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the GlobalBank Holdings Inc. Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, ladies and gentlemen, this conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the conference over to Emily Carter, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review GlobalBank Holdings's results for the Q3. With me this morning are Johnathan Hayes, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Reynolds, Chief Financial Officer; and Lisa Patel, Chief Risk Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to Johnathan Hayes.

Johnathan Hayes:
Thank you, Emily, and good morning, everyone. GlobalBank Holdings delivered solid performance in the Q3, demonstrating the strength of our diversified business model and our commitment to serving our customers.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on enhancing customer experience, driving operational efficiency, investing in strategic growth initiatives, and maintaining strong capital levels.

To give you a sense of our progress, let me start with some overall company performance highlights. This quarter, amid the Fed's 525 basis point rate hiking cycle through July, inflation above 3%, and pockets of softening in commercial real estate, we executed with discipline. Total revenue reached $7.2 billion, up 12% year-over-year and 8% excluding prior-year gains. Net interest income expanded 21% to $4.8 billion, powered by our asset-sensitive balance sheet and careful deposit repricing. Our net interest margin widened 52 basis points year-over-year to 3.42%, aided by higher yields on our $450 billion securities portfolio, averaging 4.1%, and stable deposit betas at 65% for non-interest-bearing accounts.

Non-interest revenue rose 4% to $2.4 billion, with wealth management fees jumping 15% to $950 million as assets under management climbed to $1.2 trillion, up 18% on equity rebounds. Card fees increased 9% to $525 million, fueled by 1.25 million new accounts through our GlobalBank Rewards Visa Infinite program. Investment banking fees rebounded 22% to $475 million, outpacing peers in mid-market M&A advisory.

Net income attributable to common shareholders hit $1.7 billion, up 14% year-over-year, delivering diluted EPS of $1.85—beating consensus by $0.18 and up 16% adjusted. This propelled return on tangible common equity to 15.2%, exceeding our 13% mid-cycle goal and matching top peers. Return on assets improved to 1.28%, showcasing efficient capital use.

Our balance sheet is rock-solid, with total assets at $1.1 trillion, up 6% year-over-year, and CET1 ratio at 12.1%. Loans grew 7% to $620 billion, ahead of the industry's 4% pace: C&I up 10% to $250 billion with tech and healthcare demand, investment-grade at 65%; CRE steady at $180 billion, de-risked 15% in offices with criticized loans at 2.1%; consumer up 9% to $140 billion via autos and cards. Deposits expanded 5% to $780 billion, 78% low-cost core, bolstered by 300,000 new digital checking relationships.

Credit quality is strong: net charge-offs at 42 basis points, mainly cards, below our 60 basis point cycle average; allowance at 1.28% of loans, 3.2x charge-offs.

By segment, Consumer & Business Banking delivered $3.7 billion, up 13%; Commercial Banking $2.0 billion, up 11%; Wealth & Investment Management $1.1 billion, up 16%; Markets & Trading $375 million, up 8%. U.S. operations, 85% of earnings, grew 11%, strongest in Sun Belt mortgages. Europe was flat; Asia-Pacific surged 25% on wealth inflows.

We've innovated through challenges like deposit competition and Basel III: 80% core banking on AWS, cutting IT costs 22%, real-time AI fraud detection saving $450 million; piloting tokenized deposits; 45% of $50 billion sustainability loans green-linked. Efficiency ratio at 57%, headcount at 52,000. Returning $1.05 billion quarterly via $0.45 dividend up 10% and buybacks, $1.5 billion authorized remaining. Q4 EPS guide $1.95-$2.00, ROTCE 15%+.

Shifting to net interest margin analysis, our NIM came in at 3.42% for the quarter—up 17 basis points sequentially from 3.25% in Q2 and 32 basis points year-over-year. This reflects sharp execution in asset-liability management, repricing tailwinds in rising rates with fed funds at 5.25%-5.50%, and mix shifts. Excluding excess cash at Fed yielding SOFR ~5.30%, core NIM was 3.55% on a fully taxable equivalent basis—top of peers like JPMorgan and Wells Fargo at 3.10%-3.30%.

Asset yields rose 28 basis points to 4.78%, led by C&I loans at 6.15% average, with 60% of $45 billion variable-rate resetting on steepening SOFR curve pricing 25 more basis points hikes. CRE multifamily/industrial hit 5.40% on Sun Belt originations; consumer autos steady at 7.20% via Ally partnerships; mortgages slowed at 7% rates. Securities at 3.95%, trimmed agency MBS 15% to $120 billion, shifted to 5% corporates/Treasuries.

Funding costs up 12 basis points to 1.36%, controlled with deposit betas at 42%, down from 48%, via tiered DDA pricing—28% non-interest-bearing of $320 billion deposits. Time deposits at 3.80%, wholesale at 4.50% (8% mix), better than KeyCorp/Fifth Third betas over 55%. Volumes added 5 basis points: loans +4.8% to $210 billion, deposits +3.2%, loan-to-deposit 65.6%.

Regionally, U.S. Northeast/Southeast expanded 25 basis points; Europe contracted to 2.90% on ECB 4.50%; Asia-Pacific at 3.75% on trade finance. Initiatives: $10 billion swaps floating 40% CRE, accreting 15-20 basis points; AI dynamic deposit pricing for betas <40%; green loans +75 basis points premium, 12% new C&I; non-earning assets down $2.5 billion.

NIM should hold 3.40%-3.50% in Q4, upside on curve uninversion, buffered by CET1.

Now, on credit quality metrics, our $250 billion loan portfolio shows resilience amid 5.25%-5.50% rates, 3.2% inflation, CRE softening. Under CECL, NPL ratio at 85 basis points quarter-end, down 10 sequentially from 95, 25 better than last year—lowest since 2019. Core excluding PCI at 72 basis points.

Consumer (45%): 1.05% NPLs, stable/down YoY on 15% prime digital originations, FICO 720+. C&I: 65 basis points up modestly from manufacturing/China issues, 20 below Wells. CRE (22% concentration): 120 basis points up from office in Atlanta/Charlotte, but exited $1.2 billion high-leverage, pivoted to industrial/retail >1.5x NOI.

Delinquencies 30-89 days at 1.85%, down 15 QoQ/30 YoY; autos 2.4% offset by FICO; mortgages 0.9% GSE jumbos. Net charge-offs annualized 42 basis points, down 5 QoQ, flat YoY—consumer 65 basis points cards 2.1%, commercial 18. Allowance $45 million add to 1.45% loans/285% NPLs; provision $120 million/25 basis points loans, vs. 30-40 cycle.

Southeast/Mid-Atlantic: Texas/Florida <70 basis points on energy (zero NPLs $8 billion); Baltimore CRE higher 2.8% delinquencies, cut commitments 40%. Tech edge: AI EWS on 500+ variables flags early, -22% NPL inflows; Loan Mod cures 65%, best SBA 7(a). Tightening HELOC CLTV 80%, Moody's covenants $15 billion C&I, +200 bps stress. Expect NPLs low-80s, NCOs 40-45 basis points if unemployment 3.8%; underweight CRE vs. peers.

Finally, market conditions boosted non-interest income to $2.15 billion, +14% YoY/+8% QoQ—28% of revenue vs. 24% last year, via higher-margin streams amid Fed tightening, equity/FI volatility, moderating spend.

Investment banking/capital markets $785 million +22% YoY: M&A $1.1 trillion up 9% QoQ, five >$5 billion deals like $12 billion fintech merger ($150 million fees); #4 ECM $18 billion; DCM soft -5% on 4.8% 10-year/95bps spreads, syndication $220 million. Americas 65%, US tech IPOs; EMEA +5% election/Basel; APAC 18% China H-shares.

Trading/market-making $420 million -3% YoY: VIX 18.2 boosted equities/FX/prime $180 million hedge funds on S&P 5% correction; FI -8% MOVE 105bps; equity deriv +12% Nvidia AI; commodities soft $75 oil. AI algos +15% fills/-20bps slippage, +$25 million.

Consumer/commercial $510 million +11%: deposits $210 million +9% despite caps; interchange +14% 7% volumes on Global Everyday Rewards like Chase Sapphire, spend +2.5% real; comm loans +6% 52% utilization; mortgage -25% to $85 million 7%+ rates $1.2 trillion orig, offset SLMtech +30% servicing $45 billion MSR.

Wealth/asset mgmt $435 million +18%: AUM $1.8 trillion +12% QoQ MSCI 4%; $35 billion inflows GlobalWealth AI 250k clients Robinhood APIs; GB Horizon ETFs $200 billion +22%. US +$25 billion HNW Florida/Texas; Europe $5 billion MiFID; APAC +25% Singapore/HK vs. China property.

Diversification accelerated: Stripe/Adyen BaaS $100 million FY24; $500 million quantum/blockchain JV Ripple/Polygon for RWAs 10% wealth by 2025. Q4 mid-single digits growth if VIX<20 M&A holds; 55/45 mix best-in-peer.

I will now turn the call over to Michael to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Johnathan, and good morning. GlobalBank Holdings reported net income of $1.7 billion for the Q3, or $1.85 per share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 8% driven by higher interest rates and loan growth. Non-interest income was positively impacted by diversified fee streams across markets and wealth as Johnathan outlined. We continue to maintain a strong capital position with a CET1 ratio of 12.1%. We are pleased with the progress we are making on our strategic initiatives, and we remain confident in our ability to deliver sustainable value for our shareholders.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will open the question and answer session. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Mike Johnson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson:
Good morning. Can you provide some color on your NIM expansion?

Johnathan Hayes:
Good morning, Mike. As I detailed earlier, the 17 basis point sequential pickup to 3.42% stemmed from asset repricing—particularly C&I and CRE—controlled betas at 42%, and volume growth with loans outpacing deposits. Our swaps and AI pricing tools position us for stability around 3.40%-3.50% next quarter, assuming curve dynamics hold.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Sarah Lee:
Good morning. What is your outlook for non-interest income?

Michael Reynolds:
Good morning, Sarah. We expect mid-single digit growth in Q4, building on the 14% YoY this quarter, assuming VIX stays below 20 and M&A sustains momentum. Embedded finance partnerships and blockchain initiatives should add tailwinds, supporting our optimal 55/45 revenue mix.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

David Kim:
Good morning. Can you discuss the impact of higher interest rates on your loan portfolio?

Lisa Patel:
Good morning, David. Higher rates have pressured early delinquencies modestly, especially autos at 2.4%, but our NPL ratio improved to 85 basis points, with strong provision coverage at 285% of NPLs. We've tightened underwriting—HELOCs to 80% CLTV, exited risky CRE—and our AI early warning system reduced inflows 22%. We see stabilization ahead.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to Johnathan Hayes for any closing remarks.

Johnathan Hayes:
Thank you for your interest in GlobalBank Holdings. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.

aspect_summary.Impact of market conditions on non-inter: Market conditions boosted non-interest income to $2.15B (+14% YoY, +8% QoQ, 28% of revenue), driven by Fed tightening, equity/FI volatility (VIX 18.2), and moderating spend; investment banking +22% on M&A/ECM, wealth/asset mgmt +18% on AUM growth/equity rebounds/inflows, trading mixed, consumer/commercial +11% on fees/volumes.
aspect_summary.Credit quality metrics (NPL ratio, charg: NPL ratio at 85 bps (down 10 seq from 95 bps, best since 2019, core 72 bps); consumer 1.05% stable, C&I 65 bps up modestly, CRE 120 bps up in offices but de-risked; delinquencies 30-89 days 1.85% (down 15 QoQ/30 YoY); net charge-offs 42 bps (down 5 QoQ, flat YoY, mainly cards); allowance 1.45% loans/285% NPLs; provision $120M/25 bps loans; resilient amid high rates/inflation/CRE softening due to underwriting tightening, AI EWS (-22% inflows), outlook NPLs low-80s, NCOs 40-45 bps.
aspect_summary.NIM analysis: factors influencing change: NIM 3.42% (up 17 bps seq from 3.25%, 52 bps YoY); asset yields +28 bps to 4.78% (C&I 6.15%, CRE 5.40%, securities 3.95%); funding costs +12 bps to 1.36% (deposit betas 42% down from 48%, time/wholesale higher); volumes added 5 bps (loans +4.8%, deposits +3.2%, L/D 65.6%); mix shifts/ALM execution; initiatives like swaps (+15-20 bps), AI pricing; core NIM 3.55%; outlook 3.40-3.50% Q4.
aspect_summary.Overall company performance highlights: Solid Q3: revenue $7.2B (+12% YoY), NII $4.8B (+21%), non-interest $2.4B (+4%); net income $1.7B (+14%), EPS $1.85 (+16% adj, beat consensus); ROTCE 15.2% (>13% goal), ROA 1.28%; assets $1.1T (+6%), loans $620B (+7%), deposits $780B (+5%, 78% core); CET1 12.1%; NCO 42 bps, allowance 1.28%; segments up 8-16%; efficiency 57%; capital return $1.05B/qtr; Q4 EPS $1.95-2.00, ROTCE 15%+.
